newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Devro looks to '97 with confidence.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Devro looks to '97 with confidence.

text.p: Scottish-based sausage skin maker Devro Plc is looking ahead with confidence to 1997 after the impact of so-called "mad cow disease" on several of its markets last year.

"The worst is now very much behind us and we're starting to see some improvements flow through in various markets that were affected," the company's Chief Executive Graeme Alexander told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"That was aided quite considerably, however, by the swift and positive reaction the company took in response to the issue and that really minimised the impact BSE had on the results."
Devro announced a jump in pretax profits before exceptional items for the year to December 31 of 51.9 million stg, up from 31.1 million in the previous year.
The exceptional items included a 4.5 million stg stock write-off, announced last year, in relation to BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy), or mad cow disease.

There was also a 10.5 million stg restructuring charge arising from the acquisition of Teepak International Inc in January 1996, as well as a 7.5 million stg gain from the sale of Devro America for 16.8 million stg last August.
"There are no surprises in the exceptional items, they were all well indicated in advance," Alexander said.

The company announced a rise in the total dividend to 8.5 pence a share from 7.7 pence in 1995, and a surge in turnover to 302.21 million stg -- including a contribution of 220 million stg from Teepak -- from 97.78 million.
"The results are particularly good given the fact that in the background there's been BSE and the integration of Teepak," said Alexander.
He was very encouraged by the process of integrating Teepak which he said had gone "particularly well".

Alexander said the company was looking ahead to the current financial with confidence. "This year has started off very satisfactorily...and a lot of the positive trends we saw coming through in 1996 have flowed on into 1997 and we have some considerable confidence about the future".
